full_judgment: 33. The learned second Judge, while dismissing the appeal, gave clear finding that it was manifest that Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur and Engineer Md Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Gulshan was not the same person and that the dispute regarding the title of the suit plot was started before "expiry of the Engineer Md Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza who died on 2-2-2004", whereas the plaintiff filed the suit on 8-2-2004 impleading defendant No.2, Akhtaruzzaman, a Director of Eastern Housing Limited, as the attorney of late Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza showing defendant No.1 as his vendor. The learned second Judge noticed that on 20-3-2004, 3rd party, i.e. the heirs of late Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, filed an application in the suit under Order I, rule 10 of the Code of the Civil Procedure for adding them as defendants in the suit as his heirs and not to substitute them in place of defendant No.1 stating that they got the information that the suit was filed by the plaintiff on the basis of false bainapatra created by him with fictitious person having no title and interest and possession in the suit plot, but the learned Joint District Judge by his order dated 15-7-2004 allowed the application for addition of party, not as the third party, but as the heirs of defendant No.1. The learned Judge also considered the fact that on 23-3-2004, the plaintiff by filing a fresh vokalatnama prayed for hearing the application for temporary injunction filed on 18- 3-2004 and the Court on hearing the application issued notices upon defendant Nos.1 and 2 to show cause as to why an order of temporary injunction should not be granted and on 27-5- 2004 defendant Nos.1 and 2 filed hajira and then again concluded that "So, from the record and conduct of the plaintiff it was crystal clear that defendant No.1, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur and Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157 Bara Maghbazar is not the same and one person." Considering the evidence of PW1 (the plaintiff) the learned Judge came to the findings that "it is further manifest" that the plaintiff at the time of filing the suit and sometime after, did not admit rather denied the existence, right, title and possession of Engineer Md Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar, later on only to escape and justify his earlier false activities admitted "with a device that defendant Nos.1(a) to 1(e) are the legal heirs of defendant No.1, i.e. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur" by substituting them. The plaintiff neither made a contract for purchasing the suit plot with a genuine person nor the documents submitted in Court were genuine and on the basis of those documents, he could not get decree for specific performance of contract and that the total case of the plaintiff was nothing but a got-up story only to grab the suit plot on the basis of forged deed and papers with the help of a fake person. The plaintiff failed to prove his alleged bainapatra and part payment of consideration money. The learned Judge disbelieved PWs 2 and 3 on the finding that they being employees of the plaintiff could not but oblige their master. The learned Judge also took adverse presumption against the plaintiff for non-examination of a vital and important witness, namely, Shawkat Ali, who figured as a witness in the bainapatra and lived in the same holding with defendant No.1, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza at Mirpur. In this regard, the learned Judge further opined that the identity of defendant No.1 could only be clarified by Shawkat Ali, who is also a relative of the plaintiff. The learned Judge concluded that "plaintiff not only failed to prove his own case but produced some forged and fabricated deeds and papers because from the facts and circumstances it (sic) clear that plaintiff PW.1 produced the exhibit 1,2, 3, 4 and 5 in the court showing his vendor as custodian of those exhibit's who failed to appear before the court and from the materials on record it is proved that he is none but a fake person. So, exhibit "6" (the agreement) is nothing but obviously the creation of forgery only to grab the suit property. Furthermore, the defence story and facts as set forth are quite believable not only by' oral evidences, however, facts and circumstances with possession and documentary evidences, as find support from the testimony of PWs of title suit No.81 of 2006 which has been adopted in this case with the consent of all the parties."
